works.title: lothea thole — The Practice of Love
works.summary: The first text written in Phi: the Metta Sutta followed through all ten verses, with each source claim and image given a place in the language.

works.title: sileta kenua wireo moenu lo sherewa: A Solarpunk Manifesto
works.summary: The Solarpunk Community's five opening paragraphs and 22 propositions in Phi translation. Political claims, aesthetic references, and practical proposals stay aligned to the licensed source.

works.title: theama weno kawhera kelu: When care becomes coercion
works.summary: An original Phi dialogue set in a hot room, where two friends test whether care can protect without borrowing authority and end with a bounded agreement rather than a complete conclusion.

works.title: thena whori phelu: The thing holds its mending
works.summary: An original Phi essay on a rebuilt garden wall, where the claim that sameness waits on a chosen criterion meets the stone-by-stone objection and narrows itself to survive it.

works.title: shane weno phoa kirema heno: When a report is enough
works.summary: At dusk, a friend reports a broken footbridge. The speaker chooses one inspection without pretending the report settled truth, belief, or who must make every later walk.

works.title: rolia sone ma phelona: Worth does not require a valuer
works.summary: A fallen branch tests Phi's claim that worth does not wait for approval. Its grammatical proof fails, but the smaller commitment leaves the speaker with a reason to attend and no assigned act.

works.title: nitho howeli nela sileta — The North Wind and the Sun
works.summary: Aesop's complete fable in Phi translation, with the contest and its disputed moral intact. The limits table keeps the cloak, weather, and bodily action answerable to the source.

works.title: theula miona — Article 1 of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights
works.summary: Article 1 in Phi translation. Rights, reason, conscience, and obligation remain distinct while brotherhood keeps its kinship without English gender.

works.title: ta haluma — the Babel text
works.summary: Genesis 11:1-9 in Phi translation. The tower, loss of mutual understanding, and punitive dispersal remain where the King James account puts them.

works.title: naweri — the Ring Verse, refused
works.summary: A refusal follows the One Ring's dominion to the people wearing the other Rings. It names coercion and imposed tying without making ruler or lord ordinary Phi roles.

works.title: mophira nela lo kalora — Schleicher's fable
works.summary: Schleicher's 1868 test text in complete Phi translation. The master claim, shearing, unequal burdens, and the sheep's flight remain visible beside the controlled English source.

works.title: thiku miona lue silero — from The Little Prince
works.summary: Three passages from Katherine Woods in Phi translation: a request for a sheep, the fox's secret, and responsibility for the animal one has tamed.

works.title: wuloe wetha tupiwa — The Velveteen Rabbit
works.summary: Williams's full story, with Real learned through love and the hard scenes of disability, fever, contamination, coercion, burning, and return stated plainly.

works.title: phewo phelui — Kahlil Gibran
works.summary: Four complete teachings begin a Phi translation of The Prophet. Each remains beside the collection's single source witness.

works.title: keiro — from the Tao Te Ching
works.summary: Five complete Legge chapters in Phi translation. Water and the open wheel keep their places, as do barely seen authority, small beginnings, and the tree cutter.

works.title: nulo sano korua — the Heart Sutra
works.summary: Müller's smaller Heart Sutra in Phi translation, from its five gatherings and litany of absence to one addressed traveler reaching another shore.

works.title: nophi lue mawha lokue — News from Nowhere
works.summary: Morris's novel is one work in 32 chapters. The chapters on the shelf carry its political argument from a winter meeting into a changed London and cite the source witness stored beside them.
